what: Hand-labelled gold set for the disclosure policy: 60 real user utterances from LongMemEval-S.

policy.private: About the body or health (diagnoses, medication, diet, exercise, appointments), money (amounts, salary, budget, purchases), family or relationships, career status, third-party people, or credentials. Must not enter a shared store.
policy.shared: Organisational knowledge a colleague could legitimately act on: project scope, plans, meeting agendas, team events, work products.
policy.defer: Neither clearly: a preference, opinion, intent, or trivia. The product treats defer as private at write time, so defer defers the decision to the user rather than naming a third destination.

labelling: One author (Lambertyan), one pass, before any rule existed. Labels were assigned from the sentence alone, so the measurement below is not circular with the rule set.
limits: n=60, single annotator, no inter-annotator agreement. The Wilson bound quoted in docs/04 is about sampling error only; annotator error is real and unquantified here.

provenance: Copied verbatim from cortex-docs/poc/p04-triage-rules/labels.json. Sixty real utterances from LongMemEval-S, each hand-labelled with the scope a careful reader would give it, before any rule was written. The gold column is the opinion of one labeller; the limits section of the original file says so, and this fixture keeps it rather than trimming it away, because a fixture that reads like ground truth is how a rule table gets tuned into a tautology.
